newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down in slow trade on Friday on long liquidation by retail investors, traders said.
The key March 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 3,140 yuan per tonne, losing 15 yuan. It opened at 3,150 yuan and hit a high of 3,170.
May fell 66 to 3,200, July 50 to 3,225, November fell 12 to 3,378 and the January 1998 contract 20 to 3,390. September rose 13 to 3,388.
Combined volume fell slightly to 17,100 tonnes from 17,700.
Traders said soybeans met strong resistance at high levels today and long liquidation pushed the prices down for most of the session.

"Retail investors do not want to hold positions during the coming Chinese new year holiday," one trader said. "They dominated the day's trade with most institutions staying on the sidelines waiting for market-moving news."
"The slow trading atmosphere will continue ahead of the Chinese lunar new year holiday," he added.
